name: Nishimura-Cole Indigo Selvedge Denim Jacket
description:
A classic Type III-silhouette denim jacket cut from 14.5oz selvedge indigo denim, produced by Nishimura-Cole — a small-batch label founded by two textile engineers who left a major corponation fabric division to make things slowly and correctly. The construction is traditional: single-piece back, two chest pockets with button flaps, side cinch tabs, copper rivets at stress points. The denim is sourced from a selvedge loom operation in what used to be Osaka — one of the few remaining traditional shuttle-loom facilities — and every jacket comes with a small card describing the fabric's origin run.

This jacket fades beautifully with wear. The creases and fade lines are unique to each wearer's movement patterns — the 'whiskers' at the lap, the honeycombs at the elbow, the chest fade where your bag strap rests. Nishimura-Cole produces 150 jackets per season. They sell out. The secondhand market is active and prices hold. Tier 3 buyers who care about craft own one. Tier 4 buyers who want to signal that they care about craft own one too.
what_it_says: You understand that some things improve with time and use. You're not interested in fast fashion or fast anything. The fade on your jacket is a record of where you've been.
worn_by: anyone who found one secondhand and understood what they had
story_hooks: The Osaka loom facility that produces Nishimura-Cole's denim is under acquisition pressure from a corponation textile division. If the sale goes through, the fabric changes. The label's founders are quietly trying to buy the facility themselves and need capital they don't have.

A specific jacket from Nishimura-Cole's 2194 run — identifiable by a slight warp irregularity in the right shoulder — belonged to a journalist who disappeared while investigating Spire financial flows. The jacket was found in a Tier 2 secondhand shop. Someone wants to know how it got there.

The fade pattern on a heavily worn Nishimura-Cole jacket, photographed under specific lighting, was used as an identifier in a coded message between two people who had agreed on no other contact method. The jacket's current owner has no idea.

physical_description.visual_profile: A timeless, structured denim jacket with a slightly relaxed but intentional fit. The silhouette reads as approachable and durable—neither oversized nor tailored tight. Worn by someone who values authenticity over flash.
physical_description.fit: Classic Type III cut: comfortable through the shoulders, room in the chest, tapers slightly at the waist via side cinch tabs. Sleeves hit at the wrist bone. Built for layering and movement, not constraint.
physical_description.primary_material: 14.5oz selvedge indigo denim from a traditional shuttle-loom facility in the Osaka sector. Raw, unwashed at purchase, destined to fade with the wearer's body.
physical_description.texture: Dense, slightly stiff denim with visible warp and weft. Selvedge edge visible on cuffs and hem. Copper rivets create tactile stress points. Fabric softens and develops a lived-in hand with wear—creases sharpen, indigo fades to lighter blue along movement lines.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep indigo blue, gradually fading to lighter blue and white at high-wear zones. Copper rivets and button hardware provide warm metallic contrast. Natural color variation in the denim weave.
physical_description.closures: Traditional copper buttons down the front placket. Functional button flaps on two chest pockets. Side cinch tabs with buttons for waist adjustment. Metal rivets reinforce pocket corners and stress points.
distinctive_features: Single-piece back panel (mark of quality construction)
Selvedge selvage edge visible on cuffs and hem
Copper rivets at all stress points
Provenance card included with each jacket describing fabric origin batch
Naturally develops unique fade patterns—whiskers, honeycombs, chest fades—specific to each wearer's movement and habits
Small Nishimura-Cole woven label inside neck
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 core with Tier 4 aspirational crossover. The price point and limited production (150 per season) signal craft investment. Not corpo luxury, but intentional craft that costs.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by textile engineers, independent makers, working-class professionals who value durability and beauty in utility. A quiet rejection of fast-fashion corpo supply chains. The wearer signals: I know what good construction is. I'm patient. I don't need logos to prove worth.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine and stiff when new, then progressively broken-in over months and years. High-wear jackets show clear fade patterns—indigo surrenders to white along the creases, cuffs soften, edges fray slightly. Even 'used' examples hold structural integrity. Rarely patched (the fabric is too good to discard), but may show honest wear.

image_prompt: Fashion photography of a Nishimura-Cole indigo selvedge denim jacket displayed on a dark chrome mannequin or worn by a cyberpunk model with mixed heritage features and subtle augmentations visible at wrists. Jacket photographed at 3/4 angle to show chest pockets, button hardware, and selvedge edge detail. Deep indigo fabric catches moody rim lighting in a converted Tier 3 warehouse workspace—cool blue and copper tones against concrete and steel. Close crop on fabric texture showing tight weave and natural slubs. Fade lines and whiskers visible on creases. Small Nishimura-Cole origin card propped nearby.
